title: Supreme Court & landmark cases
examples: What is the main job of the Supreme Court?
How does judicial review actually work in practice?
Can you give an example of a case that changed a law?

explain.say: Today we explore the power of the Supreme Court.
Judicial review lets courts check if laws are constitutional.
A key case established this power in many nations.
This means the courts can strike down laws that violate rights.
For example, a case might rule that free speech rights are protected.
In daily life, this power protects citizens from government overreach.

faq.q: What is the difference between a law and a constitutional right?
faq.a: A law is an act passed by a legislative body. A constitutional right is a fundamental protection written into the highest law of the land.
asks: Are rights the same as laws?
What is the difference between statute and constitution?

faq.q: Can the Supreme Court change the Constitution?
faq.a: No, the Supreme Court interprets the Constitution; it cannot rewrite or amend it itself. Amendments usually require a special process.
asks: Who has the power to amend the constitution?

faq.a: It means that a specific law or action conflicts with the fundamental principles or rights stated in the country's constitution.
asks: What does it mean to violate the constitution?
Is a law invalid if it contradicts the constitution?

faq.q: Is judicial review the same as the courts making new laws?
faq.a: No, it is different. The courts are checking if existing laws follow the rules, not creating new rules for society.
asks: Are judges making laws when they review?
Does judicial review mean the courts legislate?

faq.q: Does every country have this power?
faq.a: No, the power of judicial review varies greatly between countries and their legal systems. Some systems rely on different checks and balances.
asks: Do all countries have a Supreme Court?

facts: The Constitution is the supreme law of the land.
Judicial review is the process where courts examine the constitutionality of laws.
Landmark cases often set precedents for future laws.
The separation of powers divides government into three branches.

quiz.say: If a law contradicts the basic rights listed in the Constitution, the Supreme Court can:
quiz.why: This is the core function of judicial review, protecting fundamental rights.

wrong.0: The court must make a formal ruling, not just ignore the law.
wrong.1: Only the legislature has the power to formally amend laws.
wrong.2: While advice is given, the court has the final power to rule on validity.

quiz.say: The power to check laws against the Constitution is known as:
quiz.why: This specific term describes the judicial function of constitutional oversight.

wrong.1: This means the legislature's will is always final, which is the opposite of review.
wrong.2: This refers to actions taken by the executive branch, not the judiciary.
wrong.3: This concept suggests the legislature is the ultimate source of law.

quiz.say: When a court rules on a fundamental right, it is setting a:
quiz.why: A precedent is a past ruling that guides future decisions in similar cases.

wrong.1: A suggestion is not legally binding on future courts.
wrong.2: This word implies advice, not a binding legal requirement.
wrong.3: While helpful, a precedent is a much stronger, enforceable legal rule.
